newsitem.title: USA: California governor backs $1.5 bln bridge plan.
newsitem.headline: California governor backs $1.5 bln bridge plan.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson on Thursday endorsed a $1.5 billion plan to rebuild rather than retrofit the eastern portion of the San Francisco-Oakland Bay Bridge to withstand a major earthquake.
In a statement, the Wilson administration said the project is contingent upon an agreement between the governor and the state legislature on complete financing for the project.
"The safest and most prudent alternative from the engineering and financial standpoint is replacement," California Department of Transportation Director James van Loben Sels said.

Department of Transportation engineers said the replacement of the eastern span with a new steel-reinforced concrete skyway bridge would cost about $1.52 billion. The cost would include the retrofit of the western span.
The cost of only retrofitting the bridge had been estimated at $1.3 billion and would take five years to complete, according to state transportation officials.

For the past year, state engineers and independent seismic experts have been exploring whether reconstruction or retrofitting was the best way to provide the Bay Bridge with additional strength to withstand a major earthquake.
A 50-foot section of the Bay Bridge collapsed during the 1989 Loma Prieta earthquake.

In its statement issued in Oakland Thursday, the Wilson administration accepted the recommendation of the California Department of Transportation to replace the eastern span with a concrete bridge with five traffic lanes in each direction.

If the replacement proposal were approved by state lawmakers and cleared environmental hurdles, the Department of Transportation said it would aim to begin bridge construction in early 2000 and complete work by the end of 2003.

The department said traffic would continue using the existing structure until the new bridge opened. With the opening of the new bridge, the existing structure would be dismantled, the department said.
The San Francisco-Oakland Bay Bridge, which opened in 1936, carries an average of 280,000 vehicles a day.
State officials said the $1.5 billion bridge project would likely receive bond funds already approved by voters in addition to revenues from higher bridge tolls.
